label: a labouring man at work in his shirtsleeves in America, later 1830s and early 1840s
note: Gathered 2026-11-07 for T-3450, the 1835 labourer's working dress first worn by Patrick Mahoney (reconstructed). None is of Chicago or of Mahoney, and none is from 1835 itself: Mount's Raffle (1837) near, Weir's Wood Sawyer (1842) near, Mount's Cider Making (1840-41) far. A reference set says what a man of this role looked like, never what Mahoney wore.

pictures.name: mount_1837_raffle
pictures.from: Met open-access image DT1511 (3811 x 2812), crop [1800, 950, 2650, 2400], the man in his shirtsleeves, at full resolution
pictures.caption: William Sidney Mount, The Raffle, 1837, the man in his shirtsleeves. The Met 97.36
pictures.shows: A young working man at about a metre, to the hips: full white shirtsleeves gathered at the wrist, a buff waistcoat open at the chest, a red neckerchief knotted loose, a pale soft felt hat with a broad brim.

pictures.name: weir_1842_wood_sawyer
pictures.from: Met open-access image (1092 x 1316), the whole painting
pictures.caption: Charles E. Weir, The Wood Sawyer, 1842. The Met 2018.6
pictures.shows: A town labourer at work, whole figure at two or three metres: white shirt over a red one, a brown waistcoat worn open, dark trousers, boots, a battered black hat.

pictures.name: mount_1841_cider_making
pictures.from: Met open-access image DT72 (3811 x 3006), crop [2300, 1500, 3400, 2300], the men by the press, at full resolution
pictures.caption: William Sidney Mount, Cider Making, 1840-41, the men by the press. The Met 66.126
pictures.shows: Working men whole at a distance: white shirts, braces over the shoulders, a dark green waistcoat, full brown trousers, a red neckerchief, straw and felt hats; at this size a man reads as a pale shirt over brown legs under a hat.
